newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian energy firm hit by uncollected debts.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian energy firm hit by uncollected debts.

text.p: The National Electricity Co (NEC), which produces 87 pecent of Bulgaria's power, reported on Friday uncollected debts of some 20 billion levs until the end of January.

The NEC said in a statement the debts have added to the critical financial condition of the company, which owes more than $30 million for imported raw materials including nuclear fuel for its Kozloduy plant and spare parts for its plants.
The industrial and social sector owed more than 17 billion levs.

Deputy energy minister Ivanka Dilovska said regular government revisions of electricity prices have not kept up with a recent drastic fall of the lev against the dollar and the energy sector was suffering daily losses of $2 million.
The Bulgarian lev was traded at around 3,000 per dollar on the interbank market on Friday from 600 at the beginning of January.
The sale price of electricity has never been lower than one cent per kilowatt hour, while now it is 0.5 cents, which is too far from the required price of 3.5 cents, Dilovska told reporters.
She said the energy ministry was prepared to work under a currency board this year but not under the conditions of a hyper-inflation.
National Statistic Institute preliminary figures showed that the monthly consumer price inflation has quickened to 43.8 percent between January 1-25 from 26.9 percent in December.
